title: A cumulative wealth equation is a stock–flow identity
status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
summary: Integrating a flow defines a stock but does not determine the flow. An explicitly specified linear feedback gives a solvable growth law, a stable regime and a transparent accounting of units.
definitions: LetW(t)=W₀+∫₀ᵗ[αV(s)+βM(s)+γI(s)]ds. Each summand must have units of wealth per time.

result.statement: Forb≠0,W(t)=(W₀+a/b)e^{bt}−a/b. Forb=0,W=W₀+at. Ifb<0 the equilibrium−a/b attracts exponentially; ifb>0 it is unstable.

If the coefficients are time dependent but b(t) is prescribed, the integrating factor gives W(t)=e^{B(t)}[W₀+∫₀ᵗe^{−B(s)}a(s)ds], where B(t)=∫₀ᵗb(s)ds.
